title: Japanese-Inspired Board
seo_title: Japanese Charcuterie Board for 6–10: Umami Shopping List
description: A Japanese-inspired charcuterie board for 6–10: smoked Gouda, brie, cream cheese, wagyu or bresaola, smoked salmon, teriyaki jerky, edamame, persimmon and miso honey.
hook: Umami-forward and minimal: East-meets-West cheeses with smoked fish, wagyu and miso honey.
why: Japanese cooking is built around umami, and this board is too: smoked salmon or ikura, teriyaki jerky, miso honey and soy-glazed nuts all bring savory depth. Brie and cream cheese give that depth something soft and mild to sit on.

Fuyu persimmon or Asian pear, cucumber and pickled ginger keep it fresh, and nori, rice crackers and sesame flatbread replace the usual crackers. Keep it sparse: a Japanese-style board looks best with space around each item.

timeline.what: Take out the cheeses; mix the miso honey.
Slice the persimmon and cucumber; cut the nori.
Place the cheeses and the small bowls.
Add the salmon, beef, edamame and crackers.
Serve with sake or green tea.

faq.a: Equal parts white miso and honey stirred together. It's sweet, salty and savory, and wonderful on brie.

faq.q: Where do I find wagyu charcuterie?
faq.a: Some specialty shops sell wagyu bresaola or salami. Regular bresaola is a good swap.
Sake, a crisp Japanese lager, a dry Riesling or green tea.
